question: Antidepressant drug that can be used in nocturnal enuresis is?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Imipramine" -> "tricyclic antidepressant" -> "anticholinergic effects" -> "reduced bladder contractions" -> "decreased nocturnal enuresis" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Fluvoxamine" -> "SSRI" -> "increased serotonin" -> "no direct effect on bladder" -> "unlikely to treat nocturnal enuresis" -> 20%
CHAIN: "Phenelzine" -> "MAOI" -> "increased monoamines" -> "no direct effect on bladder" -> "unlikely to treat nocturnal enuresis" -> 15%
CHAIN: "Bupropion" -> "NDRI" -> "increased norepinephrine and dopamine" -> "no direct effect on bladder" -> "unlikely to treat nocturnal enuresis" -> 25%
analysis: Imipramine is a tricyclic antidepressant that has been historically used to treat nocturnal enuresis (bedwetting) in children. It works by reducing the frequency of urination during sleep. The other options, Fluvoxamine, Phenelzine, and Bupropion, are not typically used for this condition. Fluvoxamine is a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI), Phenelzine is a monoamine oxidase inhibitor (MAOI), and Bupropion is an atypical antidepressant, none of which are indicated for nocturnal enuresis.
